description: Multi-environment (live + demo) stickiness rule. One server hosts one environment; every call in a workflow must stay on the server that owns the referenced account.
tips: If the user says 'on demo' or 'on live', pick that environment's server explicitly.
If an account name is ambiguous, call my_portfolio on the current server first — if the account is not listed, it belongs to the other server.
Do not assume a prior answer from the other environment's server transfers here (positions, open orders, balances, alerts are all scoped to one environment).
rules: This server hosts exactly one environment — live OR demo. The two are deployed as separate MCP servers at different URLs (e.g. mcp-live.* vs mcp-demo.*), with disjoint account namespaces.
An account name is scoped to the hosting server. A DEMO account exists only on the demo server; a live account exists only on the live server. The same client may have both servers connected at once.

Within any workflow, once an account has been resolved on this server, every downstream call (my_portfolio, market_snapshot, dom_snapshot, market_history, estimate_order, place_order, modify_order, cancel_order, close_position, fill_history, order_history, order_details, position_history, daily_balance_history, cash_history, performance_summary, create_alert, list_alerts, dismiss_alert, risk_settings, update_risk_settings) must go through this same server.

Cross-routing between live and demo is a bug — it either fails (account not found) or silently targets the wrong namespace. Never resolve an account on one server and execute the downstream step on the other.
Market data is identical across environments, but fetch it via the server that owns the workflow's account so rate-limit accounting and quote subscriptions stay consistent.
